case_name: Mishrilal and others v State of Madhya Pradesh and others
facts: The four appellants along with two others were found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 read with Section 149 IPC.
They were also found guilty of the offence under Section 148 IPC.
The incident giving rise to the present appeal happened on 22.7.1990 at about 6.00 p.m.
PW-1 Kammod, PW-2 Mokam Singh and deceased Balmukund were grazing the cattle in their fields.
Appellants Mishrilal and Lallu @ Lalaram were armed with axe and A-3 Kamoda @ Kamod Singh was armed with 'lathi' while A-4 Narayan Singh was armed with a 'Luhangi.'
The prosecution case is that all of them caused injuries to deceased Balmukund.
PW 1 Kammod later went to the Police Station at Bajranggarh and gave information about the incident.
issues: Whether the incident happened after sunset and these witnesses could not have identified the assailants
Whether the evidence of PW 2 Mokam Singh was reliable
petitioner_arguments: The incident happened after sunset and these witnesses could not have identified the assailants
The evidence of PW 2 Mokam Singh was unreliable
court_reasoning: The procedure adopted by the Sessions Judge was not strictly in accordance with law.
A witness could be confronted only with a previous statement made by him.
Whenever the witness speaks falsehood in the court, and it is proved satisfactorily, the court should take a serious action against such witnesses.
holding: The appeal is without any merits and is dismissed accordingly.
cases_cited: Mishrilal and others v State of Madhya Pradesh
